今年較早前為較年幼嘅學童推出咗家長管理帳戶之後，WhatsApp 今日將家長監控功能擴展至青少年帳戶，新增咗群組活動提示同埋對 Meta AI 嘅額外限制。以下係詳細內容。

WhatsApp 擴大家長監控選項

Earlier this year, WhatsApp announced a series of new features aimed at giving parents more control over the accounts of their younger students.

These included letting parents decide who could contact the account, as well as which groups the account could join, screening message requests from unknown contacts, and protecting privacy settings on managed accounts through a parent-set PIN.

Then, a few weeks ago, WhatsApp further extended the feature to iOS, adding a dedicated "Parental Supervision" section within the Settings app to make it easier for parents to find and configure managed accounts.

Today, WhatsApp is once again expanding these supervision features — this time bringing parental monitoring to teens, not just younger students — while also giving them higher visibility into group activity and more say over how their teens interact with Channels, Status updates, and (perhaps more importantly) Meta AI.

With this update, parents can now receive notifications when their teens join or leave groups, as well as when the membership of an already-joined group grows "significantly." Parents can also now choose how their teens use Channels, who can see their Status updates, and who can view their own Status updates.

As for Meta AI, parents can now choose between the standard experience designed for users aged 13 and older, or a stricter "limited content" option, depending on what they feel is appropriate for their teen.

WhatsApp says the limited setting further restricts the topics teens can discuss with Meta AI. Meta AI features that rely on Private Processing are also unavailable when that setting is enabled.

As always, WhatsApp stresses that these parental supervision features will not allow parents to see the actual content of their teens' messages or calls, as those communications remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
